label: Accessible coverage and the dependence-to-impossibility bridge
summary: Issue #2052. Selected loss yields the existing dependence-to-impossibility premise via soundness for the shared dependence primitive, accessible absence coverage and realization of being-without by an accessible witness. A three-world omission model exhibits a case where the effect drops after the chosen removal but persists in a farther accessible world. A separate normal/repair comparison reuses the matched AND/idle mechanisms and public-input clamp, which concerns public input absence only. None of these comparisons supplies an interpretation of the existence-fact labels in the strict-ground map. Independent-review repair: witness preservation lets the selector omit accessible source-absence worlds provided it keeps an accessible contrast for each pair that has one. Full coverage entails this weaker policy, and omitting the empty near world in the same frame witnesses strictness. The sibling derivation of the modal premise uses witness preservation with the same soundness and realization assumptions.
blocker: OPEN: justify witness adequacy for real possibility and whether the same effect can persist under replacement in the sustaining scope. The dependence-to-strict-ground map still needs an independently interpreted existence-fact theory and its oriented edges.
